findings.message: The ticket requires a dormant queue (19.L CONSTRUCTION), but no criterion names the dormancy test. That test is the transitive chupa.* import-closure scan rooted at chupa/__main__.py. It must recognize both `import chupa.x` and `from chupa import x`, and it must fail once chupa/mergequeue.py becomes reachable. The Definition of rejected relies on this observable, but nothing tests it. chupa/merge.py is already reachable through chupa/runner.py, so an import of mergequeue added to merge.py would break dormancy without any test noticing.
findings.paved_road: Add a criterion: `tests/test_mergequeue.py` proves dormancy by the 19.L import-closure scan rooted at `chupa/__main__.py`, recognizing both import idioms, and the scan fails when `chupa.mergequeue` is reachable (in particular, `chupa/merge.py` does not import it).

findings.message: Sections 9 and 10 require that a worktree is NEVER left mid-rebase: every rung refusal runs `rebase --abort` before it returns. The new public stop-at-conflict op deliberately leaves a rebase in progress, so this invariant now depends on the queue's rung logic. No criterion names a test proving that every refusal path (mechanical rung refuses, strategy not declared, both rungs refuse) leaves the worktree on its own branch head with a clean status.
findings.paved_road: Add to criterion 2: on every rung refusal the worktree is not mid-rebase, HEAD equals the pre-admission branch head and `status --porcelain` is empty, proven against a real repository in `tests/test_mergequeue.py`.

findings.message: `git.py` has no public `rebase_abort`. Abort exists only as the unchecked internal `_call` inside `rebase()`. 'Preserving rebase and rebase_abort' can therefore be read as requiring a new public rebase_abort. That would be a fourth new public op, and criterion 3 forbids it ('the only new public operations are' three).
findings.paved_road: Restate it as: `rebase()` keeps its abort-before-RebaseRefused behavior unchanged (`test_refused_rebase_is_aborted_before_refusal_returns` and `test_rebase_success_does_not_abort` stay green). Name explicitly whether a public abort is in or out of the three-op allowlist that criterion 3 pins.

findings.message: Criterion 2 says only 'red-streak pause' and 'tree-hash assertion'. It drops the semantics section 9 gives them: the pause trips at K=3 consecutive DISTINCT integration-red tickets (the shipped default), and a re-red of the same ticket does not advance the streak. A tree-hash mismatch after the squash is an engine defect that escalates immediately. A test of a bare pause or assert cannot tell these semantics apart.
findings.paved_road: State K=3 (where it comes from: an engine constant or config) and the distinct-ticket rule. Name tests in which the same ticket going red twice does not trip, three distinct tickets do trip, and a tree-hash mismatch escalates instead of journaling `to: merged` as normal.

findings.message: In section 9, rung 2 is 'Full Rework', but the ticket puts Rework out of scope. 19.P3 says the mechanical rung returns a typed unresolved-conflict handoff that Rework consumes after the admission unwinds, and that it is never invoked inline. The ticket never says what the second typed rung returns. The rework-stage row, which comes later, consumes that type, so its shape matters now. Rung 1 also has no stated input: the host-declared `merge.strategies` (regenerate/union) that `chupa/config.py` already parses.
findings.paved_road: Specify both rungs. Rung 1 is mechanical: git merge plus the declared `merge.strategies` paths only, failing closed on undeclared paths. Rung 2 returns a typed unresolved-conflict handoff (a named type carrying the conflicted paths and stem) and never calls Rework inline. Add a test that selects the correct rung for each case.

findings.message: `chupa/merge.py` is fenced, but Scope in never says what changes in it. It is reachable from production (chupa/runner.py imports `merge`), and tests/test_merge.py plus eval/shakeout/merge.py exercise it. Any signature or behavior change to `merge()`, `Candidate`, `MERGE_GATES` or `PostRebaseGate` would force edits to tests/test_merge.py, chupa/runner.py or eval/shakeout, none of which are fenced (19.L rule 5, caller closure).
findings.paved_road: State what merge.py owns in this row, e.g. 'exposes the existing gate tuples for reuse; no signature or behavior change to merge()'. Declare tests/test_merge.py and tests/test_shakeout.py as preservation suites in Verification. Alternatively, if a public signature changes, fence every caller an authoring-time grep finds.
